cover.headline: 89% of AI agents never leave the pilot.

slides.heading: The blocker is not the model
slides.body: 38% of organizations are piloting agents. 11% have one in production. Leaders blame evaluation gaps, governance friction and reliability — every one of those is a harness problem, not a model problem.

slides.heading: Input 1 — The brief
slides.body: Becomes the system prompt and the permission boundary. What this agent is for, and what it may never say or do.

slides.heading: Input 2 — The journey map
slides.body: Becomes the tool allowlist and the escalation gate. Where the agent acts unattended, and where a human takes the wheel.

slides.heading: Input 3 — The measurement plan
slides.body: Becomes the eval harness and its golden-set CI gates. If it cannot be measured on a golden set, it is not a metric — it is a hope.

slides.heading: Input 4 — The segmentation
slides.body: Becomes the retrieval strategy and the recall target. Judge the corpus before you go shopping for models.

slides.heading: The harness moved the number
slides.body: Microsoft held the model constant and changed only how the system was allowed to look for evidence. BRIGHT recall@1 went from 27.8% to 49.6% — within two points of being handed the answer outright.

slides.heading: Do this next
slides.body: Write the escalation rule this week. Name the one number that proves it worked. Audit your corpus before you audit models.
